newsitem.title: KENYA: Financials boost Nairobi , but confidence low.
newsitem.headline: Financials boost Nairobi , but confidence low.

text.p: Financial stocks helped lift the Nairobi Stock Exchange (NSE) on Thursday but analysts said market confidence remained low over political uncertainty and Kenya's standoff with the International Monetary Fund (IMF).
The index edged up 8.93 points to close at 3466.92 on Thursday. Turnover was posted at 20.1 million shillings compared to 15.256 million shillings on Wednesday.
A total of 361,749 shares traded from 503,835 shares.
"There's a general lack of direction. Everyone, including foreign investors wants to sit and wait," a bourse official told Reuters.
The wait and see attitude came as Kenya awaited an IMF verdict on whether to cut off aid to the embattled east African nation over allegations of graft.
Finance Minister Musalia Mudavadi told a news conference Kenya had pleaded with the Fund to extend a Thursday deadline for it to fight corruption or lose a big aid package.
"We did ask for extra time and in that context we are waiting for an answer," Finance Minister Musalia Mudavadi said. "I am crossing my fingers."
The IMF demanded last month that the government take action to show its commitment to fight corruption and reform the energy sector or it would let the three-year aid package to lapse.
The shilling fell against the dollar and pound on Thursday because of market uncertainty ahead of the IMF decision.
Foreign exchange dealers said the Nairobi market was nervous as foreign investors and business managers awaited the IMF verdict, which was expected to be announced in Washington.
Leading stock broker John Munge of Nairobi's Shah, Munge & Partners told Reuters that foreign investors were nervous and jittery as they also awaited the IMF announcement.
"They (investors) are nervous and jittery. Today (Thursday) alone we have fielded 10 telephone calls from worried investors," Munge said.
The day's trading was centred around financial companies where investors bought in anticipation of positive half-year results. Financials accounted for 59 percent of the day's turnover.
National Industrial Credit Bank edged up to 61 from 60.50 while Kenya Commercial Bank was unchanged at 105.
Barclays Bank gained five shillings to close at 104 while Standard Chartered Bank closed at 47 unchanged. National Bank also closed at 16 unchanged.

Ever since violent clashes between riot police and pro-reform activists in early July when the market nosedived to an all-year low, foreign investor confidence had not recovered to its bullish heights, last seen in June, brokers said.
"Kenya has become hot news. People are selling," one broker said. "Everyone is holding their breath just like in the forex market," he added.
Market analysts said that this bearish tone was likely to prevail, predicting a dull market until investors received fresh signals.
In the agriculturals Brooke Bond was unchanged at 123 while Sasini Tea & Coffee edged up to 8.30 from 7.25. Kenya Airways was unchanged at 8 while Uchumi Supermarket traded at 39 from 37.50.
Kenya Power & Lighting gained a shilling to close at 175 while Kenya Breweries traded at 57 from 56.50.

The East African Development Bank corporate bond traded 2.4 million shillings at 99.42 percent from 99.92 percent while the fourth issue of the Central Bank of Kenya floating-rate treasury bond traded 30.1 million shillings at 102.3982 percent from 102.2 percent.
